foreign-keys-and-references.label: FOREIGN KEY and REFERENCES
foreign-keys-and-references.summary: Declare which parent key a child-table column points to so the relationship is part of the schema rather than only a query convention.

try_foreign_keys_and_references_sketch0.title: Link Departments to Their Managers
try_foreign_keys_and_references_sketch0.prompt: The `employees` parent table is already provided. Create a `departments` child table with its own id and name, plus a manager id that must reference an employee id. Inspect the declared relationship afterward. To test it in the workspace, run `schema.sql` before `query.sql` so the table definition exists when you inspect it.
try_foreign_keys_and_references_sketch0.hint: Leave the parent table unchanged and define the relationship on the child table.

help.concept: A foreign key records which parent key a child column may reference.
help.hint_1: manager_id is the child-side relationship column.
help.hint_2: Use SQLite's foreign-key metadata to inspect the result.

sourceCheckMessages.managerRelationship: Link `manager_id` to `employees.id` in the departments schema.

single-choice-foreign-key-purpose.title: Purpose of FOREIGN KEY
single-choice-foreign-key-purpose.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a FOREIGN KEY in a database?
single-choice-foreign-key-purpose.hint: Consider how a FOREIGN KEY maintains relationships between tables.

help.concept: A FOREIGN KEY is used to enforce referential integrity between tables by ensuring that a column in one table matches a column in another table.
help.hint_1: Think about how a FOREIGN KEY connects tables.
help.hint_2: A FOREIGN KEY ensures that a value in one table corresponds to a valid entry in another table.

options.d: To store large amounts of data

multi-choice-foreign-key-benefits.title: Benefits of FOREIGN KEY
multi-choice-foreign-key-benefits.prompt: Which of the following are benefits of using FOREIGN KEY constraints? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-foreign-key-benefits.hint: Think about how FOREIGN KEY constraints affect data integrity and relationships.

help.concept: FOREIGN KEY constraints help maintain data integrity by ensuring that relationships between tables are consistent.
help.hint_1: Consider how FOREIGN KEY constraints prevent invalid data entries.
help.hint_2: FOREIGN KEY constraints ensure that data in one table corresponds to data in another table.

drag-reorder-foreign-key-steps.title: Build the Parent-Child Schema in Order
drag-reorder-foreign-key-steps.prompt: Arrange the schema steps so a child table can reference a parent key that already exists.
drag-reorder-foreign-key-steps.hint: Create the referenced table before defining the child relationship.

help.concept: The parent key must exist before the child table definition can declare a reference to it.
help.hint_1: Start with “Create the parent table and its key”.
help.hint_2: Finish with “Declare the child FOREIGN KEY reference”.

tokens.t1: Create the parent table and its key
tokens.t3: Declare the child FOREIGN KEY reference

fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-syntax.title: FOREIGN KEY Column in the Child Table
fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-syntax.prompt: Complete the pattern: FOREIGN KEY ([blank1]) REFERENCES parent_table(parent_column).
fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-syntax.hint: The blank names the column stored in the child table.

help.concept: The FOREIGN KEY clause starts with the child column, then REFERENCES names the parent table and parent key.
help.hint_1: Look inside the parentheses immediately after FOREIGN KEY.
help.hint_2: That column belongs to the child table being defined.

fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-constraint.title: FOREIGN KEY Keyword
fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-constraint.prompt: Which SQL phrase declares a foreign-key relationship in a table definition?
fill-blank-choice-foreign-key-constraint.hint: Choose the phrase that explicitly names this relationship constraint.

help.concept: FOREIGN KEY introduces the child-side relationship before REFERENCES names the parent key.
help.hint_1: PRIMARY KEY identifies rows in the current table.
help.hint_2: UNIQUE controls duplicates rather than declaring a relationship.

multi-choice-foreign-key-requirements.title: Requirements of an Enforced SQLite Foreign Key
multi-choice-foreign-key-requirements.prompt: With SQLite foreign-key enforcement enabled, which statements about a valid foreign-key relationship are correct? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-foreign-key-requirements.hint: Focus on the parent key being referenceable and the child value having a valid parent when it is not NULL.

help.concept: The referenced parent columns must be a PRIMARY KEY or otherwise UNIQUE in a compatible way. Each non-NULL child key must match a parent key. The child column itself need not be UNIQUE or indexed for the constraint to exist.
help.hint_1: A foreign key may point to a PRIMARY KEY or an eligible UNIQUE parent key.
help.hint_2: Indexing the child key can help performance but is not what makes the relationship valid.

options.a: The referenced parent key must be PRIMARY KEY or otherwise UNIQUE in a compatible way.
options.b: Each non-NULL child key must match an existing referenced parent key.
options.c: The child foreign-key column must itself be UNIQUE.
options.d: The child foreign-key column must be indexed for the constraint to work.

practice-two-foreign-key-relationships.title: Practice: Give Order Items Two Parent Relationships
practice-two-foreign-key-relationships.prompt: The `orders` and `products` parent tables are provided. Create `order_items` so each line can identify both the order it belongs to and the product it represents. Declare both parent relationships and inspect them afterward. To test it in the workspace, run `schema.sql` before `query.sql` so the table definition exists when you inspect it.
practice-two-foreign-key-relationships.hint: The two relationship columns have different parent tables.

help.concept: One child table can carry multiple independent foreign-key relationships.
help.hint_1: order_id belongs to the orders relationship.
help.hint_2: product_id belongs to the products relationship.

sketch-foreign-key-intro.title: A foreign key protects a parent-child relationship

sketch-foreign-key-usage.title: One child table can reference more than one parent
sketch-foreign-key-usage.bodyMarkdown:
A table may participate in several relationships when each foreign-key column has a different parent role.

For example, a line item can belong to an order and also identify a product. Each relationship should name its own child column and parent key so the schema documents both paths independently.
